3120-modern-fiction.title: Modern Fiction
3120-modern-fiction.creator: Charles Dudley Warner
3120-modern-fiction.description: A book by Charles Dudley Warner. riginator of the modern novel. The older novels sprang from the poetry of the Middle Ages; their themes were knightly adventure, their personages were the nobility; the common people did not figure in them. These romances, which had degenerated into absurdities, Cervantes overthrew by "Don Quixote.

arxiv-2004-03637.title: Probabilistic Spatial Transformer Networks
arxiv-2004-03637.creator: Pola Schwöbel, Frederik Warburg, Martin Jørgensen, Kristoffer H. Madsen, Søren Hauberg
arxiv-2004-03637.description: Abstract Spatial Transformer Networks (STNs) estimate image transformations that can improve downstream tasks by ‘zooming in’ on relevant regions in an image. However, STNs are hard to train and sensitive to mis-predictions of transformations. To circumvent these limitations, we propose a probabilistic extension that estimates a stochastic transformation rather than a deterministic one.

arxiv-2503-09497.title: Federated Smoothing ADMM for Localization
arxiv-2503-09497.creator: Reza Mirzaeifard ⋆, Ashkan Moradi §, Masahiro Yukawa †, Stefan Werner ⋆
arxiv-2503-09497.description: Abstract This paper addresses the challenge of localization in federated settings, which are characterized by distributed data, non-convexity, and non-smoothness. To tackle the scalability and outlier issues inherent in such environments, we propose a robust algorithm that employs an ℓ 1 \ell_{1} -norm formulation within a novel federated ADMM framework.

arxiv-2505-00733.title: ROSA: A Knowledge-based Solution for Robot Self-Adaptation
arxiv-2505-00733.creator: Gustavo Rezende Silva 1,∗ , Juliane Päßler 2 , S. Lizeth Tapia Tarifa 2 , Einar Broch Johnsen 2 , and Carlos Hernández Corbato 1
arxiv-2505-00733.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Gustavo Rezende Silva 1,∗ , Juliane Päßler 2 , S. Lizeth Tapia Tarifa 2 , Einar Broch Johnsen 2 , and Carlos Hernández Corbato 1. Autonomous robots must operate in diverse environments and handle multiple tasks despite uncertainties. This creates challenges in designing software architectures and task decision-making algorithms, as different contexts may require distinct task logic and architectural configurations.

arxiv-2506-21102.title: Interpretable Hierarchical Concept Reasoning through Attention-Guided Graph Learning
arxiv-2506-21102.creator: David Debot, Pietro Barbiero, Gabriele Dominici, Giuseppe Marra
arxiv-2506-21102.description: Abstract Concept-Based Models (CBMs) are a class of deep learning models that provide interpretability by explaining predictions through high-level concepts. These models first predict concepts and then use them to perform a downstream task. However, current CBMs offer interpretability only for the final task prediction, while the concept predictions themselves are typically made via black-box neural networks.

arxiv-2509-16745.title: CAMBench-QR : A Structure-Aware Benchmark for Post-Hoc Explanations with QR Understanding
arxiv-2509-16745.creator: Ritabrata Chakraborty, Avijit Dasgupta, Sandeep Chaurasia
arxiv-2509-16745.description: Abstract Visual explanations are often plausible but not structurally faithful. We introduce CAMBench-QR, a structure-aware benchmark that leverages the canonical geometry of QR codes (finder patterns, timing lines, module grid) to test whether CAM methods place saliency on requisite substructures while avoiding background.

pmc-11690708.title: CHALLENGES AND BENEFITS OF HOSTING US STUDY ABROAD STUDENTS AT THE COLLEGE OF HEALTH AND WELFARE
pmc-11690708.creator: Therése Bielsten
pmc-11690708.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Aging in a Welfare State is a course with the aim of student exchange of knowledge about the Swedish and US healthcare systems. The campus week’s main purpose is to stimulate students’ reflection on their own country’s healthcare system. The week is initiated with a day of perspectives of and study visits on Growing up in Sweden to introduce US students to Sweden’s welfare system.

pmc-11710471.title: Remote App‐Based Cognitive Assessment in Aging and Pre‐Clinical Alzheimer’s Disease in a Diverse Sample of Older Adults
pmc-11710471.creator: Dawn Mechanic‐Hamilton, Valerie Humphreys, Alex Prusky, Kimberly Halberstadter, David A. Wolk
pmc-11710471.description: BackgroundMobile, valid and engaging cognitive assessments are essential for detecting and tracking change in research participants and patients at risk for Alzheimer’s Disease and Related Dementias (ADRDs). This pilot study aims to determine the feasibility and generalizability of an at‐home, app‐based cognitive assessment, the mobile cognitive app performance platform (mCAPP), to detect cognitive changes associated with aging and preclinical AD.

pmc-12512252.title: Malignant carotid body paraganglioma with nodal metastasis: a case report and review of the literature
pmc-12512252.creator: Seyedhamid Madani, Donya Rahmati, Payam Nikjo, Seyedehmahsa Madani
pmc-12512252.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundCarotid body tumors are rare neuroendocrine tumors that typically present as benign masses. However, they can exhibit malignant transformation, especially when metastasis occurs, making them a significant challenge in diagnosis and management.

pmc-12526974.title: The role of healthcare providers in sustainable return-to-work for individuals with common mental disorders
pmc-12526974.creator: Zoe Can, Cristian A Vasquez, Susan E Peters, Jeremy F Dawson
pmc-12526974.description: BackgroundMany individuals with common mental disorders (CMDs) face challenges after returning to work following sickness absence. Healthcare providers and healthcare systems are well-placed to provide returnees with support which can facilitate sustainable return-to-work.Sources of dataThis narrative review has integrated data and literature from journal articles, reports, book chapters, and official NHS and UK statistics bodies.

pmc-12548941.title: Lighting the Way: Unveiling the Mechanisms of the Photoinduced Benzyl Alcohol Oxidation Using Tailored Bismuth‐Based Perovskite‐Inspired Microcrystals
pmc-12548941.creator: Daniele Conelli, Chiara Lo Porto, Anna Moliterni, Davide Altamura, Cinzia Giannini, Fabio Palumbo, Helena Mateos, Mokurala Krishnaiah, Tuhin Samanta, Kimmo Lahtonen, G Krishnamurthy Grandhi, Paola Vivo, Gian Paolo Suranna, Roberto Grisorio
pmc-12548941.description: This study reveals that a fine balance between experimental conditions and catalyst design enhances the visible‐light‐driven oxidative process of benzyl alcohol in air. A comparative analysis of various bismuth‐based halide perovskite‐like materials with differing chemical compositions uncovers that the Cs3Bi2Br9 material outperforms the others, owing to its optimal bandgap and well‐aligned energy levels.

pmc-13412221.title: Case Report: Occipital Mature Teratoma Mimicking Encephalocele in an Infant
pmc-13412221.creator: Hannah Haile, Arjun R. Adapa, Vlad A. Korben, Phyllis L. Faust, Peter Canoll, Neil A. Feldstein
pmc-13412221.description: IntroductionIntracranial teratomas are rare congenital neoplasms that typically arise in midline structures such as the pineal and suprasellar regions. Occipital region teratomas are exceedingly uncommon.Case PresentationWe report a case of a full-term neonate born with an occipital region mass initially presumed to be an encephalocele. Postnatal surgical resection revealed a mature teratoma.

pmc-13434690.title: Occurrence of parabens in aquatic environments and sediments and efficiency of wastewater treatment plants in parabens removal
pmc-13434690.creator: Mohammad Rezvani Ghalhari, Babak Shokri, Mohammad Hadi Dehghani, Ramin Nabizadeh, Mohammadreza Khani, Kamyar Yaghmaeian
pmc-13434690.description: Parabens are endocrine-disrupting chemicals, and their entry into the human body via water sources has adverse effects on human health. In the present study, the occurrence of methylparaben, ethylparaben, propylparaben, and butylparaben in three domestic, hospital, and industrial wastewater treatment plants, and in river water and sediments, was investigated.

pmc-13473879.title: Systematic evaluation of the heterogeneity of topologically associating domain boundaries in a large genomic context in humans
pmc-13473879.creator: Ying Sun, Niels Tommerup, Lars Juhl Jensen, Jan Gorodkin
pmc-13473879.description: Topologically associating domains (TADs) are generally considered as a homogeneous basic units of genome folding, which is critical for transcriptional regulation. However, recent studies indicate that both the TAD domain structures and the boundaries between them are not as homogeneous as originally recognized.

pmc-13525039.title: Factors associated with symptom development in bilateral hip dysplasia with comparable acetabular coverage
pmc-13525039.creator: Hiroto Funahashi, Yusuke Osawa, Hiroaki Ido, Takamune Asamoto, Yasuhiko Takegami, Shiro Imagama

pmc-13561044.title: Fine-Tuning Large Language Models for Structured Extraction of Infectious Disease–Related Information From Clinical Notes in Japanese Primary Care: Development and Internal Validation Study
pmc-13561044.creator: Hiroshi Yoshihara, Haruka Maeda, Yuriko Hagiwara, Daichi Sato, Kei Kitajima, Akihiro Iwata, Nicolas Van de Velde, Yuta Nakamura, Yosuke Yamagishi, Ataru Igarashi, Javad Sarvestan
pmc-13561044.description: BackgroundThe COVID-19 pandemic highlighted the importance of timely infectious disease surveillance. In Japan, conventional sentinel and claims-based systems incur reporting lags and capture limited clinical detail, whereas free-text clinical notes in electronic health records (EHRs) hold richer, timelier symptom and vaccination information.

pmc-13593445.title: Promotion or suppression? Does internet use by the Chinese public affect physician trust?
pmc-13593445.creator: Haifeng Ding, Xinbin Xia, Jiashan Teng
pmc-13593445.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveThis study aims to explore the causal relationship between internet use and the level of physician trust among Chinese residents, providing rigorous empirical evidence for understanding the changes in doctor-patient relationships in the digital era.MethodsUsing four waves of panel data from the China Family Panel Studies (CFPS) spanning 2016 to 2022, we construct a two-way fixed effects model to control for individual and time heterogeneity.
